title: DC-area forecast: Muggy tonight with a few showers possible Saturday, then nicer
subtitle: HAPPENING NOW: Happening now: In the 70s this evening with an isolated shower or rumble possible through the overnight. Muggy lows in the upper 60s to mid-70s.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: In the 70s this evening with an isolated shower or rumble possible through the overnight. Muggy lows in the upper 60s to mid-70s.

What's next? A few showers are still possible tomorrow. Eventually, it turns noticeably cooler and less humid for the holiday weekend, and that comfortable stretch holds into early next week before temperatures climb again by midweek.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Muggy this evening with an isolated shower possible, maybe a rumble of thunder, through the overnight. Lows settle in the upper 60s to mid-70s with some patchy fog possible. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Saturday: Partly sunny with slowly decreasing humidity. But a few showers or rumbles are still possible, mainly late morning into afternoon, and especially from near DC to the west and south. Highs head for the low to mid-80s. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: A stray shower is possible but, overall, skies gradually clear as drier air filters in. Lows near 60 to mid-60s. Confidence: Medium

Sunday: Genuinely nice — mainly sunny and comfortably less humid, with highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. Confidence: Medium-High 😎 Nice Day!

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Sunday night: Mostly clear and comfortably cool. Lows in the mid-50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

The pleasant stretch continues Labor Day and Tuesday, with partly to mostly sunny skies both days, mainly low humidity, and highs near 80 to the mid-80s. Overnight lows fall into the upper 50s to mid-60s. A great setup for any holiday outdoor plans. Confidence: Medium

Temperatures trend back up starting Wednesday, with highs potentially eyeing 90 as early as Wednesday and probably surpassing 90 by Thursday as humidity slowly builds again.

DC weather history for September 4

A ferocious 1939 thunderstorm dumped nearly 4.5 inches of rain in just a couple of hours, flooding streets, stranding cars, and overwhelming basements across the city.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: Our final day of hot and humid conditions, with potentially strong storms. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
